newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BEST ON GROUND-ANDREW BARTRAM'S AUSSIE RULES COLUMN.
newsitem.headline: BEST ON GROUND-ANDREW BARTRAM'S AUSSIE RULES COLUMN.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
ORMOND-ALLEN'S BAD BREAK
The AFL has applauded the actions of Adelaide backman Trent Ormond-Allen, who named Carlton's Luke O'Sullivan as the man who broke his jaw in an off-the-ball incident at Football Park last Sunday.
O'Sullivan was suspended for the rest of the season after Ormond-Allen gave a graphic account of the incident to the tribunal on Thursday night.
The veteran Blue described the incident as a "throw-away token gesture" carried out with more exuberance than aggression.
Ormond-Allen, who crossed to the Crows from Melbourne this year, had every right to feel aggrieved because his injury will sideline him for the season and deny him a possible premiership medal.
Earlier in the week, AFL chief executive Wayne Jackson commended Ormond-Allen and Adelaide for citing O'Sullivan, saying victims of off-the-ball incidents should "stand up and be accountable".

Convention once dictated that what happened on the field stayed on the field, but not any more, especially in cases of racial vilification. Abused players have sought mediation with their accuser or justice through the tribunal this year.
ARCTIC PARK OUT IN THE COLD

The future of Waverley Park as an AFL venue looks bleak after the Hawthorn Football Club and representatives from 14 municipal councils failed to convince the League to schedule games at the maligned ground beyond the 2000 season.
The AFL is committed to the MCG, Optus Oval and the yet to be constructed Docklands Stadium and is determined to sell Waverley Park and invest the money in the new arena.
This is despite a resurgence in the popularity of the ground -- weekly attendances this season are up by an average of 8,400 spectators, or 30 per cent, on last year.
Supporters of Waverley Park have labelled the move to sell the ground as economic rationalism and ground rationalisation gone mad.
When the ground is closed football supporters to the south and east of Melbourne will have no AFL facility in their midst and will be forced to journey to the city to see live AFL football.
On the face of it, the move to close the ground will disenfranchise those supporters and, by implication, undermine some Victorian clubs whose very survival depends on the support of members.
True, the AFL once said that Victoria could not sustain 10 clubs.
LANGERS, WE SALUTE YOU
At Waverley Park this Saturday, champion Hawthorn full-back Chris Langford becomes the sixth Hawk to play 300 games when he lines up against West Coast.
The four-time premiership player, whose business commitments forced him to relocate to Sydney three years ago, captained the club in 1994.
Recruited from Melbourne Grammar before making his debut in 1983, Langford won a string of club awards and two E.J. Whitten medals for the best Victorian player in state-of-origin games.

Langford publicly opposed an attempted merger between the Hawks and Melbourne last year and defiantly removed his jumper and waved it at the crowd after the Hawks' stirring victory over the Demons in the season's final round.

Erstwhile team-mate Dermott Brereton caused a stir among Carlton officials and supporters earlier this year when he said Langford was the players' choice for full-back of the century despite Blue Stephen Silvagni gaining selection in that position for the AFL's so-called Team of the Century.
Langford's milestone and the return of Nick Holland will strengthen the Hawk line-up but not enough to overcome the resurgent Eagles, who should win comfortably.

In other games, North Melbourne will defeat an injury-ravaged Brisbane at the MCG tonight while tomorrow Western Bulldogs will arrest a four-game losing streak and beat Melbourne at Optus Oval, Collingwood will prevail over Carlton in the "blockbuster" at the MCG and Fremantle should be too strong for Richmond at the WACA.

On Sunday, Sydney will beat St Kilda and extend to 21 its unbeaten run at the SCG, Geelong will thrash Essendon at the MCG and in the South Australia derby, Adelaide should be too strong for Port Adelaide.
